source_title: Surpassing the fractional derivative: concept of the memory-dependent derivative
claim_short: Wang and Li define the memory-dependent derivative and list candidate kernels
primary_source_record: Computers and Mathematics with Applications 62 (2011) 1562-1567; primary-source PDF; Definition 2.1 Eq. (5)
scope_and_limitations: Printed p. 1562 abstract describes an integral of a common derivative over a slipping interval and application-selected kernel forms; printed p. 1563 Eq. (5) gives D_tau f(t)=1/tau integral from t-tau to t of K(t-s) f'(s) ds and specifies differentiability in t and s; pp. 1563-1564 list candidate kernels and state a general application condition 0<=K<1 on the past interval; p. 1564 Eq. (7) gives the K=1 interval-average/difference-quotient limit; pp. 1563 and 1565 describe tau as a modulatory parameter. Independent derivation: for K=1, the fundamental theorem gives [f(t)-f(t-tau)]/tau, which tends to f'(t) as tau tends to zero if f is differentiable at t. This does not verify a thermoelastic heat-flux law or a current R3F manuscript passage. The original R3B map row was read-only and not changed; this is not a new current-map mapping.
